summary: Feed s159_double to NDR is degraded: 34.6% of TCP sessions are one-way and 14.7% of frames are sliced to ~192 bytes. NDR requires bidirectional traffic and full payload for stream reassembly and detection.

findings.root_cause: 47 of 136 TCP sessions (34.6%) show traffic in only one direction, well above 10% threshold. Most likely asymmetric routing combined with single-direction SPAN or packet broker not aggregating both directions of a flow to the same NDR tool port (hash/load-balance split).
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs both directions to reassemble TCP streams, track state, and detect intrusions. One-way visibility breaks handshake analysis, flow correlation, and lateral-movement/C2 detection, causing missed detections and incomplete session records.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow/session to the same NDR port so the NDR sees client and server sides together for stateful analysis.

findings.root_cause: 264 of 1792 frames (14.7%) are cut short, most to 192 bytes snaplen, indicating packet broker slicing/packet truncation is enabled on this feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload for DPI, signature matching, file extraction and anomaly detection. Slicing at 192 bytes strips L7 payload, blinding the NDR to exploits, malware transfers and application-layer indicators.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing / set snaplen to tool MTU (9216 bytes) so the NDR receives complete frames and full payload for detection.
